structure.title: Abstract
structure.text:
Lithium ion conductors based on  $\text{Li}_2\text{M}^{3+}\text{M}^{4+}\text{P}_3\text{O}_{12}$  ( $\text{M}^{3+}=\text{Cr}$ , Fe, In;  $\text{M}^{4+}=\text{Ti}$ , Zr and Hf) have been synthesized. The  $\text{Li}_2\text{InTiP}_3\text{O}_{12}$  show larger conductivity ( $\sigma_{573~\text{K}}$  is  $1.22\times10^{-3}~\text{S cm}^{-1}$ ) in the series of compounds under study and the results are discussed in terms of the polarizability of the network cation and the unit cell volume.

structure.title: 1. Introduction
structure.text:
The low equivalent weight and the high electropositive nature of Li which gives high cell voltage and energy density of advanced electrochemical devices, paved the way for an intense search for a good Li<sup>+</sup> ion conductor with the requisite ceramic properties over the past several years. The conductivity of the compound Li<sub>3</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>2</sub>PO<sub>12</sub>, analogous to NASICON, is three orders of magnitude lower than the conductivity of the latter due to the larger tunnel size [1]. As the structure is amenable to extensive crystal chemical substitutions retaining the basic structure, by suitable modification of the framework cations, the tunnel size for Li ion migration can be modified and fast lithium ion conductors can be achieved [2–4].

Previous studies have established that substitution of a trivalent cation at the Ti site increases the conductivity of  $\text{LiTi}_2\text{P}_3\text{O}_{12}$ . The unit cell remains rhombohedral with the space group  $R\bar{3}c$  in the solid solution  $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_{2-x}\text{M}_x\text{P}_3\text{O}_{12}$  (where  $M=\text{Cr}^{3+}$  and  $\text{In}^{3+}$ ) upto x=0.8 for Cr and x=0.35 for In and

these compositions show a maximum conductivity Substitutional [5,6].studies in the  $\text{Li}_{1+r}\text{Hf}_{2-r}\text{In}_{r}\text{P}_{3}\text{O}_{12}$  system have indicated that the rhombohedral phase exists upto x = 0.3 [7]. From all the above studies it is evident that the value of x at which the crystal symmetry changes from rhombohedral to orthorhombic is dependent on the size of the tri/tetravalent cation at the octahedral site. Hence, to compare the nature of the conduction in a series of compounds with various tri/tetravalent cations, the x composition in the present study is chosen to be 1, i.e.  $Li_2M^{3+}M^{4+}P_3O_{12}$  so that all the compositions have the same crystal symmetry, viz. orthorhombic.

structure.title: 2. Experimental
structure.text:
The compounds were prepared by high temperature solid state reaction starting from the respective oxides/carbonates and ammonium dihydrogen phosphate. The final sintering temperature was 1100–1200°C. To avoid the loss of Li, the pellets were

wrapped in a Pt foil and placed in an evacuated, sealed quartz tube and heated. Phase purity is established by powder X-ray diffraction (Cu Kol, radiation) and the unit cell parameters are computed by the LSQ fit of the high angle reflections. Ionic conductivity measurements are carried out on the samples in the form of pellets which were polished with a 400 grade emery paper and Pt paint was coated on the surface and the pellets were cured at 600°C for 6 h to remove the volatile organic matter. Impedance measurements using Pt electrodes are carried out in the frequency range 100 Hz- 15 MHz between 300 K to 873 K in Ar atmosphere on pellets from the same batch and from different batches to check reproducibility of the results.
